source: NCERT Class VIII, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Polity Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. The Parliamentary System
points: India follows a **parliamentary system** of government (borrowed from Britain), in which the **executive is drawn from and accountable to the legislature (Parliament)**.
The **executive** must retain the **confidence (majority) of the Lok Sabha** to stay in power.
The **President** is the **constitutional (nominal) head**; the **Prime Minister** is the **real (executive) head**.

sections.heading: 2. The Legislature — Parliament
points: Parliament = **Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha + President**.
**Lok Sabha** — directly elected (5-yr term); **Rajya Sabha** — represents States, permanent House.
Parliament **makes laws**, controls finances (the **Budget**), and holds the executive **accountable**.

sections.heading: 3. The Executive
points: The **Union Executive** = the **President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers**.
The **President** is elected (by an electoral college) and acts on the **advice of the Council of Ministers**.
The **Prime Minister** leads the majority party/coalition in the **Lok Sabha**; the **Council of Ministers** is **collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha**.
The **permanent executive** = the **civil services (bureaucracy)**, which implements policies.

sections.heading: 4. Separation and Balance of Powers
points: The three organs — **Legislature, Executive, Judiciary** — have distinct roles and **check one another**.
The executive is **answerable to the legislature**; the judiciary can review the actions of both.
This maintains **balance** and prevents the misuse of power.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Parliamentary system: executive drawn from & accountable to the legislature.
President = nominal/constitutional head; PM = real/executive head.
Parliament = Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha + President; makes laws, controls the Budget.
Union Executive: President, VP, PM, Council of Ministers; Council collectively responsible to Lok Sabha.
Permanent executive = civil services; three organs check & balance each other.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **President = nominal head**; **Prime Minister = real executive head**.
The **Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha** (not the Rajya Sabha).
The **President acts on the advice** of the Council of Ministers.
Parliamentary system means the **executive must keep the confidence of the Lok Sabha**.
